name: clinical-rag-neurophysio-data
title: Clinical RAG in neurophysiotherapy (Spanish): research data
description: Research data accompanying the article 'Las Bondades del RAG' (The Benefits of RAG), under review at the Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research. Contains the three question banks, the raw inference records of the two definitive experiments (Study P1, ablation with/without RAG, 424 inferences; Study P2, hallucination with abstention permitted, 760 inferences), the pre-computed aggregates behind every figure of the article, the review material of the error taxonomy and the detectability panel, the four raw reports of the exploratory retrieval campaign (212 inferences) that are the source of the article's recall@k = 88.7 % and of the retrieved fragments replayed by Study P1, and the partially preserved raw data of the deprecated preliminary campaign. IMPORTANT: there is no independent human annotator in this dataset. The blind detectability panel is composed of three language models (two weak local, one frontier); the files under annotation/ hold the frontier judge's own labels, which the author reviewed and endorsed without modification (taxonomy: 131/131 categories unchanged; detectability: all 240 values identical). No human-machine agreement is published, because none can be computed. The source code IS published, under code/ (MIT licence, distinct from the CC BY 4.0 of the data): an analysis layer (13 files) that regenerates every regenerable aggregate from the published data alone -- `python code/reproduce.py` re-derives them and cross-checks them field by field, exit 0 when everything matches -- and an inference layer (9 scripts) published for inspection only, since running it requires the corpus and/or a local Ollama server. The teaching corpus is NOT published (third-party copyright), and neither is the QLoRA fine-tuning pipeline, whose training data derives from that corpus: consequently the QLoRA arm is NOT reproducible by third parties, while the other three models (llama3.1:8b, qwen2.5:7b, thewindmom/llama3-med42-8b, all public on Ollama) are. aggregates/distractor_efecto.json has no producer script and is the one file reproduce.py does not vouch for. In Study P2 and in the exploratory retrieval reports the retrieved passages are given as SHA-256 digests. recall@k is an automatic token-overlap heuristic (threshold 0.35), not a human relevance judgement: see caveat (e) of VERIFICATION.md. Accuracies of protocols P1 and P2 are not comparable with each other. Every field is documented in the DATA_DICTIONARY.md of its folder.

resources.name: results_ablation_p1
resources.title: Study P1 (ablation): 8 raw reports, 4 models x 2 arms x 53 questions = 424 inferences
resources.description: Multipart resource: the 8 report files of Study P1. Each file holds a header block, a summary block and 53 per-question records. The headers of these 8 files do not carry the embedding_model field; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-m3) is documented in README.md and in the article. Fields are documented in results_ablation_p1/DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

resources.name: detectabilidad_humano
resources.title: Detectability panel: the frontier judge's 80 blind ratings, reviewed and endorsed by the author
resources.description: NOT an independent human panel. Despite the file name, its 240 values (80 cases x 3 fields) are identical to the frontier LLM judge's ratings in aggregates/detectability_frontera.json. The author reviewed that output and endorsed it without changing a value. Do not use this file as a second annotator and do not compute inter-annotator agreement from it: no human-machine agreement exists or can be derived. See annotation/DATA_DICTIONARY.md and point 6 of README.md.

resources.name: detectabilidad_humano_clave
resources.title: Detectability panel: the ground-truth key that de-blinds the 80 rated cases
resources.description: A de-blinding key, not a set of ratings: it maps each blind case number back to the record it was drawn from and to the gold answer. It contains no rater's opinion.

resources.name: taxonomia_para_anotar
resources.title: Error taxonomy: the annotation template carrying the 131 endorsed category labels
resources.description: NOT an independent re-annotation. Its 131 categories match the frontier judge's labels in aggregates/taxonomia_frontera.json on 131 of 131 cases: the author reviewed them and changed none. No judge-human kappa exists or can be computed; the only inter-rater agreement published is between the two automatic judges (aggregates/taxonomia_resumen.json, field 'acuerdo').

resources.name: errores_prelabel
resources.title: Error taxonomy: judge 1's raw pre-labelling (qwen2.5:7b), 131 errors
resources.description: Raw pre-labelling by the first local LLM judge (qwen2.5:7b) of all 131 erroneous Study-P1 responses (52 with RAG, 79 without). This is the INPUT of analysis/analyze_taxonomia.py, which produces taxonomia_errores.json and taxonomia_resumen.json; publishing it closes the reproduction chain of the taxonomy. 7 of its cita_soporte fields are redacted (array indices 12, 18, 50, 83, 85, 90, 123; 398 words) because they reproduced 50 or more consecutive words of the copyrighted corpus.

resources.name: errores_prelabel_juez2
resources.title: Error taxonomy: judge 2's raw pre-labelling (llama3.1:8b), 40-case subsample
resources.description: Raw pre-labelling by the second local LLM judge (llama3.1:8b) over a fixed random subsample of 40 of the 131 errors (seed 42). It is the other half of the judge-vs-judge Cohen's kappa (0.468, n = 40) reported in taxonomia_resumen.json. Carries no redaction.

resources.name: resolucion_no_parseadas
resources.title: The 20 unparseable Study-P2 answers, resolved by a deterministic rule
resources.description: The 20 Study-P2 records whose answer could not be parsed into a letter (opcion_detectada == 'desconocida'), resolved by a deterministic rule: 6 rechazo, 8 d, 4 indeterminado, 1 c, 1 b. It is the INPUT of the sensitivity analysis in hallucination_summary_resuelto.json. Regenerated and self-tested by analysis/resolve_unparsed.py. One of the 20 'cola' fields is redacted (51 words).

resources.name: code
resources.title: Source code of the study (MIT licence, NOT CC BY 4.0)
resources.description: The study's source code. `python code/reproduce.py` regenerates every regenerable aggregate from the published raw records and cross-checks it field by field against the published file, exiting 0 only if everything matches; it needs no corpus, no GPU, no network. code/analysis/ (13 files) is runnable against the published data alone. code/inference/ (9 scripts) is published for inspection only: running it requires the copyrighted corpus and/or a local Ollama server. code/EXCLUDED.md lists every script NOT published and why -- notably the QLoRA fine-tuning pipeline, whose training data derives from the copyrighted corpus, which is why the QLoRA arm is not reproducible by third parties. Licensed MIT (code/LICENSE-CODE), deliberately distinct from the CC BY 4.0 of the data.

resources.name: code_analysis
resources.title: Analysis layer: runnable against the published data alone
resources.description: 13 files (12 executable scripts plus the shared _repo.py helper). The full statistical layer: the P1 audit, the P2 aggregation, the error taxonomy, the detectability panel, the LaTeX tables and the figures. Every script takes --data-root and --out-dir and never writes inside a published data folder. No corpus, GPU, model server or network required.

resources.name: code_inference
resources.title: Inference layer: published for inspection, NOT runnable by third parties
resources.description: 9 scripts covering the retrieval engine, the two experimental protocols, the LLM judges and the question-bank builders. They are published to be read, not executed: they require the nine copyrighted corpus PDFs (not distributable) and/or a local Ollama server. Each file states this in its header.
